_notes: game_state added locally, from a 4-player game played through the cabinet's streamer.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent in CPU RAM at 0x000309FC and 0x000309FD, player low
and ball high. The player byte completed 1->2->3 three times, once per ball; the ball byte once.
Scores are 4 bytes on 4-byte centres from 0x021109E4 -- the same base as 24, X-Men, twd_156c and
Avatar, but 4-byte spacing where 24 and Avatar use 8. Base and stride vary independently across
SAM and neither can be assumed from the other.
Confirmed after the table exited: the map decodes that game as 4 players scoring 1,257,870 /
1,235,240 / 862,190 / 1,062,330. The DMD's 'HIGH SCORE #4  P P  25,000,000' also matches the
Fourth Place entry this map already declared.
game_over, tilted and credits come from a 900-frame recording of live memory spanning two games
with a tilt on the first game's ball 1. The scores were reset on exit and did not persist, but
the tap captures live memory during play, so the fields are unaffected.
0x00030A2E is the trn_174h/avr_200 status bitfield at ball+0x31: 1 in attract, 19 in play, 21
tilted. game_over (mask 0x12, inverted) is correct in all 900 frames across both games; tilted
(bit 0x04) marks exactly the eight samples from the tilt to the end of the tilted ball, during
which player 1's score sat frozen at 46,420. Third game to use this offset+encoding.
credits at 0x0211100C, the fifth SAM game measured at that address.
The byte briefly reads 0 late in the recording where the operator reset NVRAM; that decodes as
game over, which is correct for that moment, and does not affect the mask.
